hyps.why: Node 1's only input is edge 0, so replacing none revives node 1 and both its outgoing paths, a far larger gain than swapping one live op for another.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 outputs zeros, so a conv on edge 1->3 adds nothing.
With edge 2->3 removed, node 2 never reaches the output, so improving its input edge has no effect.
Edge 1->2 only matters through edge 2->3; if that edge is none, the conv is wasted.
Adding a residual skip where there was none improves gradient flow and connectivity, whereas replacing an existing op such as a conv gains little or loses capacity.
Replacing the direct input-to-output 3x3 conv with an identity throws away learnable capacity, unlike replacing weaker ops.
Removing a 3x3 conv from the deepest path to the output hurts much more than removing a pooling or skip op.
Swapping the strongest op for parameter-free pooling costs much more than swapping in pooling for none or skip.
With edge 1->3 already removed, cutting edge 0->3 leaves the output fed only through node 2, which risks a nearly disconnected or very shallow cell.
Turning an absent direct edge into a 3x3 conv adds a whole new useful path, a bigger gain than upgrading an existing skip, pool or 1x1 op.
